levels.lead: What software architecture is and how to practise it: requirements, quality, design, documentation and analysis. Fourteen lessons, a hands-on lab, five timed mock exams and readiness guidance for the iSAQB Foundation exam.
levels.why: Most people learn architecture by absorbing it from the one or two systems they have worked on. levels.title: Agentic AI Architecture
levels.lead: Design systems where AI agents do real work: tools, memory, limits, evaluation and human approval, documented so the next engineer can trust them.
levels.why: An agent is a system component that makes decisions at run time, which changes how you design, test and secure everything around it. This level treats agents as architecture, not as a feature: what they may do, what they must never do, how you know they work, and how you stop them. Its scope is informed by current research and the iSAQB CPSA-A AGENTA module, Architecture for Agentic Software Engineering Contexts; Intellica’s curriculum and credential remain independent.
levels.needs: Level 3, Quality, Decisions and Evaluation, or equivalent experience designing systems against quality goals.

courses.title: Application Cyber Security for Agentic Environments
courses.lead: A professional 28-lesson course in application cyber security for agentic environments. Learn to secure agents that interpret untrusted content, use tools, retain memory, delegate tasks and execute code. This is the online course for Level 2 of Intellica’s Cyber Security Academy.
courses.why: Agents read untrusted text and then act: they send, spend, change records and run code. That makes the model the wrong place to rely on for safety. This course is built on one rule: the model may propose an action, but independently enforced policy decides whether that action is allowed to affect the world.
courses.needs: Working knowledge of software or IT systems. Written for engineers, security practitioners and technical leads.

course.headline: Secure the agents you run, as a course you take at your own pace.
course.lead: Twenty-eight concise lessons across seven modules, each with a worked case, field guide, three recall questions and a guided lab. The 28 lab steps build one assurance pack for an agent system you know. The course is aligned primarily to Levels 2 and 3 of the Cybersecurity Academy, with supporting lessons mapped across all six levels.
course.honesty: This is self-study: every lesson includes a field guide, worked case, knowledge check and guided lab, with a model solution and rubric for self-review. The course completion certificate records progress reported by your browser; it is not proctored, your lab work is not independently marked, and it is not an accredited qualification.

method.title: Short lessons you control
method.text: Short slide lessons, each with a transcript. Move at your own pace and go back whenever you like.

method.title: One growing assurance pack
method.text: After every lesson a lab asks you to write real security work for your own agent system: threat model, identity design, containment plan, detection rules, incident runbook. The 28 sections join into one pack you download at the end.

method.title: Frontier research, with sources
method.text: Lessons 21 to 28 teach what 2026 papers and incident reports changed: adaptive attacks, enforcement outside the model, containing your own agents, measuring poisoning, honest detection, MCP authorization, skills and identity. Every figure cites the page it came from.

method.title: Practice tools you can run
method.text: A policy tester and a trace spotter run in your browser, and a local reference lab kit (one Node file, no network, synthetic data) mounts seeded flaws against a reference control and an unsafe baseline. Fixtures and the Rego policy download with them.

method.title: A worked case and a field guide
method.text: Every lesson has a case to read and practical guidance to apply, so the ideas are tied to decisions you will actually make.

method.title: Mark your own work
method.text: Each lab has a model solution and a four-criterion rubric. Score yourself 0, 1 or 2 on each, then close the gaps. The health check only confirms the pack is complete.

method.title: Pause and recall
method.text: Three questions at the end of each lesson, with the reason for each answer. Your progress is stored in this browser only.

evidence: Retrieval practice and spacing are among the best-studied learning techniques, so each lesson ends by asking what you remember before it shows you.
